This is a remastering process where all of the various sounds in a song are distorted so that they are at the same amplitude. To me, this ruins the songs by removing the contrast of high and low sounds. There's just no impact from things that should have impact. Also, it doesn't make sense for drums to be the same amplitude as the singer!

The compression wars have been going on for some time. People are using 3 band and up compressors that work on different frequency ranges. They're really nifty devices that don't have the bad side effects of single band compressors. Like everything else, moderation is the key. Listen to a CD from a well known old time mastering engineer and the music will still sound nice despite the EQ and compression.

Sometimes a ton of EQ is required to get the music to sound natural. You would be surprised at how many recordings you think sound natural have tons of processing.
